tool_args.rationale: The high-gradient rows establish a strong sign-changing downturn, while the Hill-2/linear-bleed candidate failed fresh confirmation. The barrier-modulated siphon law is a distinct stationary four-parameter candidate that combines gradient inhibition with a signed square-root branch; the existing eight rows support numerical fitting without another probe.

considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: The observations all have the same H and the reversal is already evident in the expanded gradient range; the immediate failure is mechanism mismatch, not short-horizon ambiguity.

considered_alternatives.option: Hill-2 competitive inhibition with linear bleed
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: This was already fit and fresh confirmation refuted it (RMSE 0.404, well above tolerance); its large training error also indicates poor fit.
Its nonnegative peak-and-decline form cannot naturally represent the observed strongly negative outputs without an additional mechanism.
